name: hh-meanrev-micro: post-shock vol-contraction re-entry (5m)
rationale: MECHANISM: two-stage. A washout spikes realized vol, then vol MEAN-REVERTS (contracts toward baseline). The tradeable snapback is NOT at the instant of the spike (too much adverse-selection / knife-catching) but as vol_realized ROLLS OVER from its peak — the point where forced flow is exhausted and makers re-tighten spreads. At entry the other side is the last stop-outs; the fader waits for the vol-contraction confirmation to avoid buying mid-cascade. This persists because vol clustering plus vol mean-reversion are among the most robust stylized facts in crypto, so 'enter the fade only after realized vol turns DOWN from an extreme' is a mechanically-grounded, less-crowded timing rule than raw bb_z. Entry: bb_z extreme (dislocation present) AND vol_realized crossing DOWN through a fitted level (contraction confirmed) AND rsi below a floor (still oversold, room to recover). Long-only spot; exit as bb_z reverts. DISCONFIRMER: if waiting for vol-contraction does NOT beat entering at the spike (the delayed entry just misses the bounce and earns less net), the timing refinement is dead. LEAKAGE guard: 'vol turning down' must be computed strictly from CLOSED bars — re-run with a 1-bar lag; if the edge vanishes it was look-ahead, kill.
catalyst: fade entered only as realized vol rolls over from a post-washout peak
